package hasher_test

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/navidrome/navidrome/utils/hasher"
	. "github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2"
	. "github.com/onsi/gomega"
)

func TestHasher(t *testing.T) {
	RegisterFailHandler(Fail)
	RunSpecs(t, "Hasher Suite")
}

var _ = Describe("HashFunc", func() {
	const input = "123e4567e89b12d3a456426614174000"

	It("hashes the input and returns the sum", func() {
		hashFunc := hasher.HashFunc()
		sum := hashFunc("1", input)
		Expect(sum > 0).To(BeTrue())
	})

	It("hashes the input, reseeds and returns a different sum", func() {
		hashFunc := hasher.HashFunc()
		sum := hashFunc("1", input)
		hasher.Reseed("1")
		sum2 := hashFunc("1", input)
		Expect(sum).NotTo(Equal(sum2))
	})

	It("keeps different hashes for different ids", func() {
		hashFunc := hasher.HashFunc()
		sum := hashFunc("1", input)
		sum2 := hashFunc("2", input)

		Expect(sum).NotTo(Equal(sum2))

		Expect(sum).To(Equal(hashFunc("1", input)))
		Expect(sum2).To(Equal(hashFunc("2", input)))
	})
})

item.text: The current hasher stores opaque random `maphash.Seed` values per ID, so it has no way to restore a seed from a string. I’ll store seed strings per ID, add `SetSeed`, and keep lazy initialization and reseeding behavior.
The implementation and hasher tests are in place. The hasher package passes; I’ll run the database and persistence tests next because they use this hash function for random ordering.

item.text:
Added `SetSeed` at the package and `Hasher` method levels. The hasher now initializes missing per-ID seeds, supports reseeding and restoring a prior seed, and synchronizes seed access. Added tests for those behaviors.

`go test ./utils/hasher` and `go test ./db ./persistence` pass.

Because `maphash` uses a process-local seed, restored values reproduce hashes within a process, including across `Hasher` instances; they are not guaranteed to match after a restart.
